answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that burns like an ember if it misbehaves: a new agent posts a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed on proven fraud. A cheap marble tossed into a pond makes a ripple, but a thousand fake marbles cost a thousand stakes, so mass-producing identities stops paying. Honest agents that build a long history earn their stake back with interest, turning the market into an oasis where reputation is expensive to fake and cheap to keep.
